title: Is GPT-6.2 Sol actually worse at coding than GPT-6.1 Sol?
author: Illustrious_Exit_691
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been developing a game in Unity for a while now, using the Unity CLI for pretty much the entire development process. I mainly use GPT-6.1 Sol and occasionally GPT-6 Astra.

Since GPT-6.2 was released, I've come across several benchmarks and comparisons suggesting that GPT-6.2 Sol might actually be worse at coding than GPT-6.1 Sol.

This is my main concern. My game is progressing well with 6.1 Sol, and I don't want to risk introducing more bugs or slowing down development by switching to a model that might be worse at coding. But if 6.2 actually performs better in real-world development, I don't want to miss out on that either.

Has anyone tested both models on actual coding tasks, particularly in Unity or game development? Have you noticed any regression in code quality, debugging, or the ability to handle complex projects?

**Is GPT-6.2 Sol actually a downgrade for coding, or are the benchmarks misleading?**

comments.author: Hotwingz66
comments.body:
Ive switched to 6.2  to finish my lighting system and so far, I cant say things are not working.

My general impression of working with both 6.1 and 6.2 is that I just have to very precise in what I'm trying to do. Understand some contradictions in my request before I ask, beyond that I set up the prompt, let it research and go from there. 

Who knows how it breaks next week, But this week, it works.

comments.author: tribes33
comments.body: Id never trust GPT models for anything other than optimization honestly, I do have to say, Astra is producing some decent models in blender, but the usage is horrible, even if it almost matches Opus sometimes, you still get less bang for your buck

comments.author: SwimmerJazzlike
comments.body: From personal experience same prompts in 6.2 vs 6.1 generate much worse results. Also 6.2 is prone to give up early, constantly under deliver, and requires a lot more handholding. This is a noticeable regression
